Westlands School
Welcome to Westlands School, where our well-established reputation for success is built on an inclusive, nurturing and aspirational learning environment.
At our school, traditional values concerning personal responsibility, excellent behaviour and hard work are combined with a strong sense of community that encourages kindness and care for one another. This ethos is encapsulated by the school’s RADAR system which promotes Respect, Achievement, Diversity, Aspiration and Resilience.
Our staff lead by example and work hard to ensure that our students feel happy, valued and secure. The proactive pastoral care and support we provide means that student wellbeing permeates throughout our school.
High-quality teaching and learning and a rich curriculum provides our students with opportunities to develop as independent learners and allows them to progress no matter what their background, learning needs, gifts or talents. As a large school we are able to offer a wide range of facilities and courses to appeal to students who are academic, creative, and practical. There really is something for everybody.
Academic progress, especially in literacy and numeracy, is a top priority. Our results suggest that we are right to emphasise these key skills, as our students’ academic success and the progress they make has been noted through successive OFSTED reports and in the Performance Tables year after year.
I hope that our website provides you with a flavour of what Westlands School has to offer. But I would encourage any prospective parents and students to come and visit us, when possible, during the school day, to see for yourself why we are so proud of the students and staff who make up our school community.

pageCache.text:
Home
Brilliant GCSE and BTEC Grades!
We are delighted to celebrate the fantastic achievements of our Year 11 cohort in this year's results. Their commitment and perseverance have truly paid off, leading to brilliant grades across a wide range of subjects.
We are proud to report an impressive increase in the number of Grade 8s and 9s awarded across all our GCSEs. With our students achieving significantly more top grades this year in English, Mathematics, Science, and History! This success is also reflected in our vocational subjects, where well over a quarter of our Child Development and our Sports students achieved a Dist or Dist*.
It is wonderful to see the progress and attainment of our Year 11 students continue to be a real strength, with a clear link between their hard work and their brilliant results.
We would like to congratulate each of our students for their well-earned achievements and wish them all the very best for their future studies.

pageCache.text:
Home
Brilliant GCSE and BTEC Results!
We are delighted to celebrate the fantastic achievements of our Year 11 cohort in this year's results. The hard work, commitment, and perseverance demonstrated by the Class of 2026 have truly paid off, leading to outstanding outcomes across a wide range of subjects.
Our students have made excellent progress and achieved results that are even higher than last year! Not only was there an impressive increase in the number of students securing pass grades in core subjects, including English, Mathematics, and Combined Science, but this upward trend was also reflected in our creative and humanities subjects, such as Geography, Media Studies, and Drama, as well as across our practical subjects, including Engineering, Animal Care, and Dance.
It is wonderful to see the progress and attainment of our Year 11 students continue to be a real strength, with a clear link between their attendance, their attitudes to learning, and their fantastic results.
On behalf of everyone at Westlands, we want to say a huge congratulations to all of our Year 11 students. Thank you to our staff for their excellent support, and to our parents and carers for working alongside us every step of the way.
We wish the Class of 2026 every happiness and success as they take their next steps into Sixth Form, college, and apprenticeships!

pageCache.text:
Home
Celebrating Our Sixth Form Students!
We are immensely proud of all our Key Stage 5 students following another year of excellent academic and vocational performance. Their excellent work ethic and resilience have led to brilliant grades, with fantastic results across A Levels, T Levels, and BTEC qualifications.
Academic excellence was evident across all pathways, with over a third of all A Level results awarded at A*-B grade, an increase in Distinction* grades for our Level 3 BTECs, and an incredible 73% of our students studying ‘tech level’ qualifications achieved an A*/A equivalent or Distinction/Distinction*.
Over half of our Class of 2026 are now heading to university, with 100% of applicants securing their first-choice destinations—including prestigious Russell Group institutions.
Our heartfelt congratulations go to all our hardworking students on these impressive achievements. We wish them every success as they embark on their university courses, high-quality apprenticeships, and exciting future careers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Westlands School - Kent School Award for Resilience and Emotional Wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Home
Kent School Award for Resilience and Emotional Wellbeing
We are absolutely delighted to share some wonderful news with our school community.
Westlands School has officially been reaccredited with the Kent School Award for Resilience and Emotional Wellbeing.
This award, supported by the Kent Resilience Hub, is a testament to our ongoing commitment to the mental health and emotional wellbeing of both our students and our staff. In their feedback, the awarding body praised the "wide-ranging programs and resources" we have in place, noting that “wellbeing is truly part of our core daily work.”
The award is more than just a certificate on the wall; it reflects the daily culture at Westlands. By achieving this, we have demonstrated that:
Resilience is embedded in our teaching, helping students develop the tools to navigate challenges both inside and outside the classroom.
Student voice is prioritised, ensuring that our young people have a say in how wellbeing is managed within their school.
Support systems are robust, providing clear and effective pathways for any student who may need extra help.
We are incredibly proud of our students, whose maturity and openness regarding mental health continue to inspire us. We also want to thank you, our parents and carers. Your partnership is a vital part of the "whole-school approach" that this award celebrates.
As we move forward, we remain dedicated to sustaining and embedding these principles into everything we do. We believe that a happy, resilient child is a child who is ready to learn and succeed.
Thank you for your continued support in making Westlands a nurturing and supportive environment for all.

Careers
At Westlands School, we understand the importance of careers education for all students in Year 7 through to Year 13. The careers provision we offer seeks to deliver on the Department for Education Careers Statutory Guidance (January 2018). Westlands School is working to achieve the 8 Gatsby Careers Benchmarks, which reflect international best practice, to improve careers provision.
In addition to our links with local universities, through being part of the Kent and Medway Progression Federation (KMPF) we are working closely with the Careers and Enterprise Company, who regularly advise us as we work towards the Gatsby Benchmarks which set out best practices for all schools across the country.
Within the school we have progressed further with careers initiatives by introducing our Careers Hub. This is a fantastic space dedicated to careers which includes software and prospectuses. Our careers hub is available for students at lunchtimes and after school.
Before school, at lunchtimes and after school on a Thursday the careers team will be available to speak to students about future plans and aspirations and are able to answer any questions that students might have regarding their next steps. Parents and carers are always welcome to contact Mr Gregory, our Careers Leader, to seek advice and ask any questions they might have regarding career pathways.
Our series of employer encounters ensures we have a variety of guests coming to the school to speak to students about a range of careers and interesting experiences.
If you would like to come and deliver a talk to students as part of our employer encounters programme, or you would like to be part of our Careers Fair, please contact the Careers team.
All information on our Careers section will be reviewed and amended during Term 6.

Modern Foreign Languages
Modern Foreign Languages
Subject Leader: Mrs J Chainey
If you wish to learn more about our curriculum please contact the Subject Lead by clicking on their name above.
Pupils study French and Spanish in Years 7 and 8 on a carousel basis. They continue with one language in Year 9.
Key Stage 5
A Level French
Our French A Level course aims to transform our students from citizens of Sittingbourne to citizens of the world. We will liberate them from insularity and expose them to other cultures, broadening their horizons and equipping them with the language skills to enable them to study or work overseas. It will give students the opportunity to develop their writing, reading, speaking and listening skills in the target language, to learn about the political, historical and social background of the country whose language they are studying. They will experience another culture, its art, literature, music and film.
Assessment: 100% examination to be assessed in the final year of the course.
Listening, Reading, Writing – 50%
Key Stage 4
GCSE French and Spanish
GCSEs in French help pupils develop their language skills in a variety of contexts and gives a broad understanding of the culture of countries and communities where French is spoken. It encourages enjoyment of language learning and recognises that language skills enable pupils to take their place in a multilingual global society.
Pupils study the specification from the beginning of Year 10. It requires them to develop their ability to write and speak in French and to understand French when it is written down or spoken. This qualification counts towards the English Baccalaureate (Ebacc). Pupils in Year 11 study the following themes on which the assessments are based. 1: Identity and culture. 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest. 3: Current and future study and employment.
Equal weighting for all four skills - Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing.
Assessment: 100% examination to be assessed in the final year of the course.

Joining Westlands

Open Morning Tours 2026
Open Morning Tours 2026
Monday 28 September – Friday 2 October 2026
Tours run daily from 9.00am to approximately 10.15am.
If you want to see what a typical day at Westlands School is like, our Open Morning tours are the perfect way to do it. These tours offer a unique opportunity to see our school in action during a normal school day.
The tour will begin at 9.00am with a short talk from our Headteacher. Afterwards, a Senior Leader will take you on a guided tour of the school site in a small group. You will have the chance to go into lessons and see our teachers and students at work, giving you a real sense of our purposeful and happy environment.
Our tours are not rigidly planned; your guide can take you to the areas that interest you most, from our academic departments to our specialist facilities. During your visit, you will have the opportunity to see:
Students actively engaged in lessons across a range of subjects.
The atmosphere in our corridors and communal areas during unstructured times.
Our new farm building and science classrooms.
The everyday use of our extensive facilities, including our sports hall, new on-site gym, library, and DT workshops.
Seeing our school 'up and running' is the best way to understand our values and get a true sense of what makes Westlands School such a special place to learn and grow.
To book your place on an Open Morning Tour, please contact the Westlands School Office by calling 01795 477475 or emailing westlandsoffice@swale.at.
We look forward to showing you around.

Young Carers information
We have many students at Westlands School who are registered young carers, and we believe there are potentially more students who may meet the criteria of a young carer, but they are not yet registered.
At Westlands School we have a dedicated team who act as a point of contact and advocate for our young carers. They are trained to identify, support, and refer young carers to appropriate services, ensuring they receive the necessary assistance to manage both their education and caring responsibilities. Please see the details of our young carers champions below:
Miss K Donegan - Young Carers Lead
Mrs A Giles - SLT Young Carers Lead
Mrs K Payne - Young Carers Champion
Miss E Tilley - Young Carers Champion
What is a young carer?
A young carer is someone under 18 who cares for a family member with a disability, illness, mental health condition, or substance abuse issue.
If you believe your child falls within the above criteria, please click one of the links below to register your child as a young carer to get them the additional support they may need.
All registered and engaging young carers of secondary/college age from 11-18yrs (including those moving up to Year 7 from September) are entitled to apply for a free KCC Travel Saver and 16+ Travel Saver bus pass as long as they are not 18 or older at the start of the academic school year.
The link for parents/carers to apply for either Travel Savers is: KCC Travel Saver - Kent County Council.
Young Carers Lunchtime Club
We host a Young Carers lunchtime club facilitated by our safeguarding team on the first Wednesday of each month from 12.40pm - 1.15pm in the Resilience Room.
The club is open to any young carer so they can come along to make new friends by meeting other young carers, socialise and gain additional support.
It is a non-judgemental, safe space where young carers can be themselves and have fun! Activities that take place at the lunchtime club include: arts and crafts, board games and more.
Westlands School works closely with the support services of Crossroads (Swale) and Imago (Kent and London) to support our young carers.

Crossroads Care Kent is dedicated to supporting unpaid carers in Kent by providing quality services that allow them to maintain a life of their own outside of their caregiving responsibilities. They strive to keep families together and ensure that carers have access to the breaks and support they deserve, enabling them to continue their invaluable role in society. Through their tailored services and advocacy efforts, they empower carers to live fulfilling lives while caring for their loved ones.
How does Crossroads Care Kent support young carers?
They provide one-to-one support, group activities, holiday outings, emotional support, family assistance, skills workshops, school liaison, and information and guidance.

Kent Young Carers (KYC) is the service provider for Young Carers aged 5-18 across Kent (excluding Medway). Young Carers are taking on caring responsibilities for a family member with a long-term illness, disability, mental health or substance misuse issue.
KYC works with schools, communities, and statutory and voluntary agencies to identify hidden young carers. Following assessment, KYC offers a range of short-term interventions including signposting, one-to-one support, in school support and workshops.
How does Imago support young carers?
During school holidays, they provide activity days for young carers. The activity days give the young carer respite from their caring role and an opportunity to experience new activities.
Targeted emotional support is offered alongside respite care, with mental health workshops and well-being sessions led by a trained counsellor. Imago and Crossroads can also refer individuals to one-to-one counselling sessions when needed. They have an open-door policy where anyone they support can always find a listening ear.
They offer one-to-one support to address the evolving needs of young carers, tackling issues such as confidence building, self-esteem, and facilitating access to specialist services. Additionally, in times of crisis, they offer young carers one-to-one sessions, to enhance their well-being.
Regular group nights provide young carers with opportunities to socialise, make new friends and have time away from their caring role. Activities include resilience building, healthy eating activities, football, arts and crafts, board games, and Nintendo Wii. It's a non-judgemental space where they can be themselves. Refreshments are provided for a comfortable experience.
They also offer advice and guidance for families in relation to the young carers caring role.
